resources.string: Apps in the protected space are kept separate from the rest of the phone under Android protection.

Android will show the required system screens. After the space is created, open the briefcase-badged Liberty app and install the apps you need from the protected-profile store. They will be kept separate from personal-profile apps.

Optional. Choose a Google Account through the Android system window. It stays in your personal profile and can make Play, saved passwords, and passkeys available inside the protected space. Liberty never receives your password or stores the account address.
Choose an account for the protected space
Android could not open the Google Account picker. You can continue without it.
A similar protected area already exists on this phone, or the firmware does not support this feature. Liberty changes nothing without your confirmation.
Apps in the protected profile are kept separate from the rest and open through Liberty.

Tap “Open protected space”. Configure the settings you need. Find the folder on your phone that contains apps with briefcase badges. To isolate apps, do not tap “+” inside this folder. Install the apps you want to isolate through the briefcase-badged Google Play icon at the bottom. After installation, the matching app shortcut will disappear from the regular home screen.
Automatic opening did not work. Find the briefcase-badged Liberty app in your app list — that is your protected space.
Some Android launchers do not switch protected areas automatically. Open your app list and tap the briefcase-badged Liberty app.
Liberty will open its protected copy. Confirm removal of the space and all of its apps and local data there. Android will then offer to remove the personal Liberty app.
In the protected Liberty copy, tap “Remove protected space”. If it does not open, find the briefcase-badged Liberty app.
Liberty does not transmit data outside your phone.
No VPN in Liberty · No data transmission · Separate apps and accounts
Android did not confirm every isolation rule. Restart Liberty. If the warning remains, do not launch protected apps on this device.
Liberty will not open the app until Android confirms every required isolation rule.
Liberty checks the protected profile connection type locally.
Android reports no VPN or HTTP proxy in the protected profile. Apps can be opened.
Android reports a VPN or HTTP proxy in the protected profile. Liberty has temporarily blocked app launching.
Liberty could not confirm a direct connection. Check Wi‑Fi or mobile data.
Liberty will not open the protected app while Android reports a VPN or HTTP proxy, or while the active network cannot be determined.

Liberty will open the system store inside the protected profile. Apps installed there are separate copies with a briefcase badge. Do not use the “+” in a system folder: on some phones it opens the personal copy and does not guarantee isolation.

Use this if there is a risk that your phone may no longer be near you. Protected apps will close immediately. The next time you enter, Android will ask for the password you set for the protected profile.
For maximum protection, set a separate Android passcode for this space. Liberty cannot read it.
Android confirmed that the protected space now uses a security code. Liberty never receives or stores it.
There are no isolated apps yet. Tap “Install apps” and install the app you need from the protected-profile store. It will appear here as a separate briefcase-badged copy.
The app store for the protected space could not be opened.
The space could not be locked. Check the separate system passcode.

Liberty manages only the protected space it creates to separate its apps from the personal profile.
This app signature does not match the Liberty release certificate. Creating and managing the protected space has been blocked for your safety.
Язык можно изменить позже в Liberty.
You can change it later in Liberty.
Liberty is built around data minimization. It requires no registration and creates no user account.
Liberty has no internet permission, includes no advertising, analytics, or trackers, and sends no personal data, app list, or user activity to the developer or any third party.

Your language choice and acknowledgment of this policy are stored on the phone. Liberty does not store a list of protected-space apps. Before launching an app, Liberty locally checks whether Android reports a VPN or HTTP proxy on the active network; the result is neither stored nor transmitted. If you choose, Liberty temporarily receives the selected Google Account name from the system picker and passes it to Android provisioning; Liberty never receives the password or stores the account name.

With your explicit confirmation, Liberty asks Android to create a separate system area (a work profile) and applies isolation policies. Liberty can open the system store inside the protected profile, but it does not install apps without user confirmation. Liberty cannot read passwords, personal data, or protected-app content.
Apps in the protected space operate under their own terms and privacy policies. Their network traffic does not pass through Liberty.

Only after your explicit confirmation can Liberty ask Android to remove the protected space it manages. This deletes its apps and local data, but not personal-profile data. You can also remove Liberty through Android system settings. The policy is available at liberty.crinoidea.net/privacy.

This removes the entire Liberty protected space. The operation cannot be undone after confirmation.
All apps, accounts, files, and local data inside the protected space. Your personal profile and its data will not be affected.
Make sure you have saved any receipts, files, or other data you need. The space cannot be restored after removal.
